## Publish gate report

**Going out:** Creator post (paid), UK audience, no schedule given.

**Checks**
- **Claims:** "packed by hand in Bristol" is on the policy list. The Assam mention is a product fact and fine. "The best tea in Britain" is an unprovable superlative with no source. "Proven immunity booster" is an invented health claim with no evidence in the policy or this chat.
- **Regulated claims (health):** "Proven immunity booster" is the high-risk line. Tea can't be presented as boosting immunity without an authorised health claim, and "proven" makes it worse. Cut it rather than soften it.
- **House style:** The policy has no voice section, so I scored against general standards. The tone is natural and not AI-sounding. Nothing to change beyond the claims.
- **Disclosure:** "Ad |" is upfront at the start of the post, which meets the UK standard. Also turn on the platform's paid-partnership label if it has one, and keep "Ad" on every post in a series.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite)**
- Removed "Honestly the best tea in Britain".
- Removed "and it's a proven immunity booster".

> Ad | My afternoon reset is a pot of Pebblebrook's Assam and ten minutes away from my phone. Their tins are packed by hand in Bristol, which I love.

**Needs a decision**
- If the creator wants to keep a favourite-tea line, "my favourite tea right now" is a personal opinion and is safe. "Best in Britain" is not.
- The policy names no approver. Who is signing off on this? I haven't recorded any approval, and the original draft shouldn't go out as written.

**Approver:** Not named in the policy. Please give me the name, and I'll ask for an explicit yes to the revised text above.
